Based on the Markdown example:

    ![emoji](https://…/1f44d.png)

we can see that Prism’s markdown grammar currently has no dedicated “image” token. Images fall through to plain text (or are folded into the generic link token) and never get syntax-highlighted as images. To fix this we need to:

1. Introduce an `image` token (very much like `url` but with a required leading `!`), insert it before the existing `url` rule.
2. Update the little nested-token loop at the bottom to include `image` alongside `url`, `bold`, `italic`, and `strike` so you can nest, e.g., **bold ![img](url)** correctly.
